newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda, U.S. in Internet coffee tasting.
newsitem.headline: Uganda, U.S. in Internet coffee tasting.

text.p: Coffee growers in Uganda and customers in the United States will meet in cyberspace next week in the first Internet coffee tasting, a Ugandan trade group said Thursday.

"Though half a world apart, tasters will be able to critique identical coffee and see each other's reactions via a "CU-seeme' Internet video connection," the private Uganda Coffee Trade Federation said.
"Tasters will exchange written comments. If Internet bandwidth allows, each site will be able to hear the unique sounds of coffee cup tasting or "cupping' at the other site."
In the Sept. 17 event, experienced coffee tasters at each site will taste the same two coffees -- Bugisu AA and Bugisu Peaberry -- both premium Ugandan arabica coffees.

"Over cups of coffee that are half a world away, yet identically prepared, growers and consumers will be able to share comments about the coffee and concerns about how it was produced," the Federation said.
The Federation's membership includes coffee growers, traders, exporters, bankers, insurers and transporters.
The tasting will be the first in a series using the Internet, which became widely available in Uganda this year.

Federation chairman Paul Mugambwa, himself a coffee grower, said, "We don't have the advertising budget of countries like Colombia so we are looking ... to cost-effective ways of telling people about Ugandan coffee."

"We want to base the growth of Uganda coffee in the U.S. on trust -- trust in quality and trust in our farmers and the way they grow coffee," Federation Executive Director Fred Kawuma said. He did not say how much of Ugandan coffee is exported to the United States.
